The test image shows the **underside of a soybean leaf** with:
- A grayish-blue, somewhat powdery/felty coating over the leaf surface
- Small yellowish-green spots visible
- The wrinkled/puckered texture typical of fungal colonization on the abaxial surface

This is classic **Downy mildew** — the grayish sporulation (sporangiophores) on the underside of leaves is the hallmark diagnostic sign, corresponding to the yellow spots visible on the upper surface. The reference image confirms yellow spots on top; the test image shows the corresponding grayish sporulation on the underside.
